description: This project will strengthen Ghana's cyber security capability and resilience by supporting the professionalisation of the cyber workforce, enhancing institutional capability within key national cyber security institutions, and deepening practical UK-Ghana collaboration on cyber policy, regulation and operations. title: MTN Ghana US$1.1 billion three-year Ghana capital-investment programme (2026–2028)
description:
**US$1.1 billion equivalent over a three-year period (2026–2028)**, announced by MTN Group
President and CEO Ralph Mupita at a media interaction in Accra on **2026-02-20** during a
three-day working visit, and published by MTN Ghana on **2026-02-23**: "We are going to
accelerate capital investment within the business, US$1.1 billion equivalent over a three-year
period to build robust infrastructure. Previously, we invested US$1 billion over five years."
Purpose: network infrastructure, 4G/5G coverage, data centres, fibre and home broadband, and
customer experience, under MTN's Ambition/Mission 2030 strategy. **US$380 million of it is
stated for 2026**, alongside ~800 new network sites (MTN Ghana CEO Stephen Blewett, 30th
anniversary launch, MTN House Accra, 2026-05-14; restated 2026-07-31). The announcing party
denominates in USD-equivalent in its own words while reporting in cedi.

*This record was built 2026-07-23 from a Daily Graphic report of a 2026-07-20 statement by
MTN Ghana's Chief Home Officer Richard Acheampong putting the figure at "US$1 billion" for
digital infrastructure with no timeframe. **Reconcile, 2026-08-01, resolved that against the
company primary**: the US$1bn is MTN's **superseded five-year prior**, and the July restatement
of it does not describe a second commitment (see* `## Notes`*). The legacy* `deal_id`
*(`mtn-gha-fibre-home-2026`) and filename are kept unchanged so existing links hold, though the
programme is wider than fibre and home broadband.*

title: Africa Data Centres Ghana — Accra ACC1 Data Centre (30MW, DFC-Backed)
description: Africa Data Centres announced in May 2023 construction of its first Ghana data centre at the Ghana Trade Fair Redevelopment Project in Accra's Central Business District. The facility is designed for initial 10MW (expandable to 30MW), built in partnership with Onix Data Centres (partnership confirmed June 2024). The investment is part of ADC's DFC-backed $300M facility; in October 2023 ADC and DFC signed a statement reaffirming their partnership, with DFC signalling intent to mobilise approximately $50M (15% of $300M) of the existing DFC facility for Ghana. Investments covered: (1) 400 2G sites, 400 3G sites, and 1,142 4G sites deployed, reaching 99.3% 4G population coverage; (2) 820 4G site upgrades; (3) IT systems modernisation; (4) MoMo platform capacity improvements. Revenue from Mobile Money grew 11.6% to GHS 1.9bn. MoMo active users reached ~11 million by end 2022. title: China Eximbank provides $218.4 million concessional loan for ICT-Based Distance Learning Project for 5 National Tertiary Education Institutions
description: According to the Government of Ghana’s Development Cooperation Management Information System (Gh-DCMIS), China Eximbank and the Government of Ghana's Ministry of Education signed a $218,490,000.00 concessional loan agreement for the ICT-Based Distance Learning Project for 5 National Tertiary Education Institutions on October 30, 2020. The borrowing terms of the loan are unknown. The purpose of the project is to provide technical solutions that connect the satellite campuses of covered public universities and Centre for National Distance Learning and Open Schooling (CENDLOS) to the nearest Vodafone Fiber Connection Node to build up a distance learning and internal university network.  The Gh-DCMIS identifies the project’s originally expected commencement and completion dates as October 30, 2020 and October 31, 2025, respectively.

title: China Eximbank provides $39 million concessional loan for ICT Enabled Distance Learning Project for the Institute of Local Government Studies
description: According to the Government of Ghana’s Development Cooperation Management Information System (Gh-DCMIS), China Eximbank and the Government of Ghana signed a $39 million concessional loan agreement for the ICT Enabled Distance Learning Project for the Institute of Local Government Studies on October 30, 2020. The borrowing terms of the loan are unknown.   The purpose of the project is to establish ICT-based facilities to provide and support distance learning for the Institute of Local Government Studies to carry out effective and efficient distance learning education and training services for public sector workers and organizations. The Gh-DCMIS identifies the project’s originally expected commencement and completion dates as October 30, 2020 and October 31, 2024, respectively.  There are some indications that the China Eximbank loan for the ICT Enabled Distance Learning Project may be financially underperforming vis-a-vis the original expectations of the lender. According to the World Bank’s International Development Statistics, the Government of Ghana had accumulated principal and interest arrears to one or more official sector Chinese creditors worth $908,337,346.70) in 2020 ($763,228,526.60 in principal arrears and $145,108,820.10 in interest arrears). Then, on December 19, 2022, the Government of Ghana announced a sovereign default. suspending debt service on its Eurobonds, its commercial loans, and most of its bilateral loans.

title: MTN Ghana (Scancom PLC) 4G 800MHz Spectrum Licence — NCA Auction
description: MTN Ghana (operating as Scancom PLC) was the sole winner of Ghana's National Communications Authority (NCA) 800MHz spectrum auction in December 2015, acquiring 2x10MHz of 800MHz LTE spectrum for $67.5 million. This was Ghana's first 4G spectrum auction and MTN paid the minimum reserve price, as the three other potential bidders withdrew. The licence enabled MTN Ghana to become Ghana's first 4G operator, launching commercial 4G LTE services in early 2016. MTN deployed additional $18M in site infrastructure for the launch. As of 2021, MTN Ghana had 3.4 million active 4G subscribers and a 82% 4G market share.
